Title: Call a friend
Description: Trust us, they want to hear from you <3

Title: Snuggle a pet
Description: Don't have one? Go get one and make a day of it!

Title: Cuddle your favorite stuffed animal
Description: Why do we rob ourselves of this freedom as adult? Reclaim the beauty of your inner child.

Title: Self holding
Description: Place your hands on the opposite sides of your face and breathe deeply

Title: Play an instrument
Description: Bang a piano or strum a guitar until you've expressed all you can with it. Any instrument will do. Let the universe hear you.

Title: Smell something
Description: Take in a deep breath of a smell you like. At the grocery store approaching a panic attack a once stopped to smell an orange for a few seconds. It wasn't magic, but it helped.

Title: Call a parent
Description: If you have a parent you trust, consider calling them. It's awkward at first but I like to ask "will you still love me if x..." and then I share the anxiety inducing thought I'm struggling with. Even though you both know what their answer is, let them say it. Let yourself hear it. I promise they will love saying it, give them a chance to.

Title: Tend to a plant
Description: Water a plant. Research how to care for your specific plant. Don't have a plant? Do you want one? Consider making an event of getting one.
Needs: Need for all living things to flourish,Nurturing

Title: Share your strategies!
Description:
No one likes unsolicited advise (unfortunately), but you can share your strategies here for others to find when they are looking for them ;)
It would make our lives so much more wonderful if you did!
Needs: Need for all living things to flourish,Contribution

Title: Try Meetup
Description: Meetup is a website that tries to connect you to people with similar interests. Worth a shot?

Title: Crunch the numbers
Description: This isn't for everyone I know, but I like to review my budget. I made a google sheet of my expenses vs my income. Having a clear plan really does calm my nerves.

Title: Stare off
Description: Sit or lay down and just notice everything your body is feeling. I like to start with my toes and work my way up to my forehead while I'm just staring off. Reminding myself where I am in the world.

Title: Listen
Description: Listen to someone speak and before you answer, try to get in touch with their underlying need first. Often I find when the help I offer doesn't *actually help* my need for contribution is frustrated. Try to avoid offering help until it's be explicitly requested. Instead, listen for their underlying need and try to connect to that.

Title: Write
Description: I like to get some kind of words on a page. Even if it's garbage I find the process can help.
Needs: Self expression,To be seen,To be heard,Need to matter,Autonomy,Authenticity,Integrity,Acceptance ,Honesty,Growth

Title: View previous things you've written or made
Description: To no one's surprise I often understand myself better than anyone else. Sometimes in a crisis I'll read something I wrote a month ago and think "yes that's exactly it!" - like past me is giving empathy to future me.

Title: Make art
Description: Whatever kind. A scribble, a drawing, a painting, a piece of music.

Title: Clean something
Description: Clean your room, your kitchen, anything. Bring order to the chaos :)

Title: Go on walk
Description: I know you probably hear it a lot.. but going on a walk really can make a fascinating difference.

Title: Listen to music
Description: A lot of variety available to you here. Could benefit from calming music or raging music. You do you ;)

Title: Make a request in conversation
Description: Often in conversation if I’m hearing something as a demand I say something like “I’m needing some autonomy I think because I’d like to be free to disagree but I’m afraid that might sound to you like criticism.” It’s not perfect but it’s something to honor what’s alive in me.

Title: View art that you connect to
Description: Whether it’s in your house, online, or at an exhibit sometimes you find a piece of art that moves you - like it understands you on a profound level.

Title: Play a video game
Description: There is such a wide diversity of video games out there. Calming exploratory games, puzzle games, combat, story, single or multiplayer, etc. Once I get in touch with the need that is alive in me it’s fun to look for a game or game genre that might tend specifically to that.
Needs: Acknowledgement,Freedom,Belonging,Inclusion,Community,Contribution,Control,Choice,Clarity,Causality,Act Freely,Need to matter,Friendship,Relaxation,Authenticity,Autonomy,Rest,Mattering,Beauty,To be seen,To be heard,Do things at my own pace and in my own way,Accomplishment,Growth

Title: Road trip
Description: Long or short it doesn't matter. Drive around the block in silence or with music. Maybe plan a trip somewhere.
Needs: Freedom,Act Freely,Choose Freely,Autonomy,Control,Choice,Safety,Do things at my own pace and in my own way,Privacy

Title: No Man's Sky
Description: For me this game is calming. Just go harvest resources and float through space. I like to name things to as a way to feel like I'm making a difference or matter because there is a tiny chance someone someday will land on the planet and see all the names.

Title: Schedule your day
Description: Consider using pictures if lists are unhelpful. Could draw them or print them. It's not perfect but having some kind of a plan can help me

Title: Reduce Mental Tasks
Description: If you end up with a list that is overwhelming then see if you can give yourself freedom to reduce or combine tasks. For example if you can’t seem to work out regularly because of the anxiety of counting reps or planning routines consider watching a guided youtube video or finding a gym that offers a trainer. Be honest and try to let any shame leave your body if you can. We can’t all do everything like everyone else :)

Title: Play a social video game
Description: Some games involve other human interactions, corporatize games are sometimes called “PVE” (player vs environment) but other games that have compelling fictional characters could also be nice. Similar to reading a book you can build relationships with the characters and find connection in relating to their experience.

Title: Read a character driven novel
Description: When we read a book the world and it’s inhabitants can feel especially personal. We can build very powerful connections this way and can go a long way in helping us feel less alone in the world. It’s okay for those relationships to mean so much to us, that’s why the author worked so hard on them <3

Title: Mindfulness (Trust)
Description: Reflect on moments you’ve reliably done what you intended to. From things like getting out of bed (eventually) to doing chores or keeping a promise to a friend. Every moment you make it through, each next breath you take, you prove to your friends and family that you can be trusted to keep living. If someone is not able to extend trust to you it doesn’t have to mean you are untrustworthy. It just means they have a need too which is not being met for some reason. I find when I engage my thoughts this way it’s easier to have compassion on myself and others.

Title: Write a letter
Description: To a friend or a senator. Advocate for yourself or others.

Title: Compassionate meditation
Description:
Reflect on decision you made that you regret and listen for the need you were trying to meet. Leave room to grieve how tragic it is that in that moment no better strategies came to mind. 
Do the same exercise reflecting on past pains you’ve endured from others. Consider what need was not met for you when they did or did not do a specific thing. Honor the need that wasn’t met. Consider what need they have had and grieve how tragic it is that no better strategies came to mind for them in that moment - strategies that could have included your needs.

Title: Make a list and check things off
Description: If you make the tasks small enough so as to avoid becoming overwhelmed the experience of checking something off a list can be very powerful. Things like “10 minutes playing piano scales” or “10 minutes cleaning the kitchen” are a great start. Set a timer and allow yourself to feel repeat when the ten minutes are up. Don’t force yourself to go past these simple goal. Enjoy having make a goal and achieved it.

Title: Watch a comfort show
Description: Try to make space to watch a tv show or movie that feels something like home for you.

Title: (Honor) Reflection Meditation
Description:
Reflect on moments this need has been met in the past. Was it an award you received? Verbal affirmation from a loved one? Consider calling a trusted friend and making a very vulnerable and specific request. "I'm wondering if you could tell me that even though I haven't accomplished some of my dreams, I am still beautiful person whose existence adds value to the world?" 
Consider also if you can validate that in yourself sometimes, perhaps regularly. Reflect on art your proud of, or the children your proud to have raised, the obstacles you're overcome in life, and see if you can honor yourself in some way by meditating on those things.

Title: Request a clear request
Description: Consider asking someone to share a vulnerable and specific request with you? Call a friend or loved one and vulnerably share that you really are just wanting to make life wonderful for them but you're unsure how. Make clear that you are looking for requests that leave out all ambiguity. Ask if they would share what needs are alive in them and imagine ways you could contribute to *one* of them.

Title: Charity work
Description: Consider looking for charity work in your area. Find a soup kitchen for the homeless or a local nonprofit doing work you believe in. Even just walking along picking up trash truly does make life more wonderful for your entire community - even if only in some small and sacred way.

Title: Sing
Description: Find a private place to sing as loud as you’re comfortable. Sing with your favorite song in the car or if you play an instrument you could play a song you know. Search for a hymn online and sing that.
Needs: To be heard,Self expression,Autonomy,To be seen,Empowerment,Mattering,Need to matter,Control

Title: Read a poem you like aloud
Description: Try a search online like poets.org. Search a key word related to what you’re experiencing right now. Find a poem you’re relating to and in the privacy of your room or car or closet (wherever you feel comfortable) and read the poem aloud to yourself. Let it gives you words in a time when you have none. Experience the validation that this artist understands also how you might be feeling right now and sees it as valid too.
Needs: To be heard,Acknowledgement,Belonging,To be seen,Need to matter,Serenity,Beauty

Title: Stand Largely
Description: Take a wide stance, place your arms up high and apart. Making a sort of X shape with your arms and legs take up as much space as possible. Trying this for about 30 seconds. We know that the postures our bodies takes often represent our emotional state and, interestingly, research suggests that this system can also work in reverse. Give your body space and see if it helps give your psychological date space too.

Title: Volunteering / Acts of Kindness
Description: Tend to the life in others. Looks for ways that seem like trustworthy strategies to truly make life more wonderful for others. Sometimes we find that serving life in others turns out to serve life in us as well. Be careful to truly hear and identify what someone is needing before you try to do something you think they'd enjoy as it can turn out to be especially discouraging to have tried to make life wonderful for someone only to realize they were needing something else altogether. Make space for them to share their needs and make a clear request or seek out volunteer work that are confident really is doing good work.
